name: Home landing rail inset
reason: The full width desktop rail has no inset while the narrow rail retains 16px gutters.

name: Home destinations rail bleed
reason: The destination border and background extend to the full rail width while its text keeps the page gutter.

name: Home destinations inset
reason: The destination text aligns to the same responsive page gutter as the home cards.

name: Compact home display size
reason: The existing home Display treatment uses a compact size below 820px and remains a named exception to semantic heading roles.

name: Compact home display leading
reason: The compact home Display treatment preserves its established line height.

name: Compact home subtitle
reason: The existing home hero subtitle returns to Body size below 520px.

name: Responsive desktop navigation cluster
reason: The desktop navigation row contracts continuously to fit intermediate widths before it is replaced by the mobile menu.

name: Compact public logo
reason: The existing compact header needs a shorter brand wordmark beside its location label.

name: Compact public location label
reason: The narrow header preserves the existing location label fit at 520px and below.

name: Home image fade geometry
reason: The translucent edge tracks the home hero image at different wide viewport widths.

name: Chrome wide rail alignment
reason: Header and footer align within the existing 1600px chrome rail while retaining edge clearance.

name: Fixed bottom navigation clearance
reason: The mobile navigation has a fixed 62px hit area and page content needs matching bottom clearance.

name: Resizable map panel width
reason: The map keeps a usable minimum area while the investigation panel can be dragged.

name: Wide resizable map panel width
reason: Wide screens reserve at least 600px for the map and for the panel.

name: Mobile sheet grip height
reason: The drag grip occupies a fixed region used by sheet position calculations.

name: Mobile sheet peek height
reason: The compact sheet leaves a readable preview above the map.
